gristmillr

gristmillr is an httr2-based client for the Grist REST API. Functions take a lightweight document handle first and return data frames, so they compose with pipes.

This is a development version; see NEWS.md.

Setup

Set your API key (and, for a team or self-hosted site, the server) in .Renviron:

GRIST_API_KEY=<your key>
GRIST_SERVER=https://myteam.getgrist.com

Or pass the key to grist_doc(api_key = ), as a string or as a function such as \() keyring::key_get("grist"). Keys given as strings are never saved with the object.

Usage 

library(gristmillr)

doc <- grist_doc("<doc id or URL>")
grist_tables(doc)
#> # A data frame: 2 × 3
#>   id     table_ref on_demand
#>   <chr>      <int> <lgl>    
#> 1 Table1         1 FALSE    
#> 2 People         2 FALSE

doc |>
  grist_records("People", filter = list(status = "active"), sort = "-age")
#> # A data frame: 2 × 4
#>      id name    age status
#>   <int> <chr> <int> <chr> 
#> 1     1 Ann      31 active
#> 2     3 Cy       28 active

data.frame(name = "Dee", age = 52L, status = "active") |>
  grist_records_add(doc, "People")

grist_sql(doc, "SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM People GROUP BY status")
#> # A data frame: 2 × 2
#>   status      n
#>   <chr>   <int>
#> 1 active      3
#> 2 pending     1

To move data in or out, grist_export() writes tables to Parquet, CSV or JSON files with a data-dict description of their columns and references, and grist_import() loads them into another document. See vignette("migrating-data") for moving data in from other tools.

See vignette("gristmillr") to get started and vignette("joining-tables") for working with reference columns.

Coming from gristapi

The gristapi package is built around an R6 object. gristmillr has no stateful objects: the document handle holds only an ID, a server and request settings, and every function takes and returns data frames.

gristapi gristmillr
listtables() grist_tables()
listcolumns() grist_columns()
fetch_table() grist_records()
countrows() grist_count()
add_records() grist_records_add()
update_records() grist_records_update()
delete_records() grist_records_delete()
sync_table() grist_records_upsert() (key_cols is by)

Other differences:

  • Cell types are converted from column metadata by default, with convert = "basic" and "raw" as alternatives.
  • Settings that rarely change live in grist_request_options(), grist_read_options() and grist_write_options().
  • gristmillr also covers documents and workspaces, schema changes, SQL, downloads, attachments, webhooks and document history.
  • It does not depend on dplyr, tidyr or sf.
